headline: Asensio out for 3 months, and the derby stays close
summary: Marco Asensio will be out for around 3 months after knee surgery, beIN Sports report, and Fenerbahçe's week did not get easier: they led Slavia Prague on Tuesday and drew 2-2. Galatasaray arrive at the Intercontinental derby top of the Süper Lig — 1st place, 19 points — after a 4-2 win at Lille. Yet Fenerbahçe average 2.57 expected goals a game, the chances they create, and across the market average the hosts are 42.5% favourites. The handicap makes Galatasaray only 0.25 goals better, and the main goal line of 3.25, with over at 47.4%, points to goals.
read: The Intercontinental derby pits the league leaders against a Fenerbahçe side that has just let a two-goal lead slip in Europe and lost Marco Asensio to knee surgery, with Nathan Ake also an injury doubt. The market makes Galatasaray clear but not overwhelming favourites at 42.5%, rates them only about a quarter of a goal the better side, and expects an open game of around three goals.

facts.fact: Galatasaray top the Süper Lig with 19 points from eight matches.
facts.meaning: They are three points clear of Fenerbahçe in third from the same number of games, so this is a genuine top-of-the-table derby.

facts.fact: Galatasaray won 4-2 away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, twice coming from behind for their first points of the campaign.
facts.meaning: They go into the derby on a win in Europe's top competition rather than on the back foot.

facts.fact: Fenerbahçe drew 2-2 at home with Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Tuesday after leading 2-0.
facts.meaning: They come into the derby having let a winning position slip, still chasing a first European win.

facts.fact: Marco Asensio will be out for around three months after knee surgery, having played through the injury.
facts.meaning: Fenerbahçe lose a senior attacking option for the derby and for the rest of the autumn, not just for one match.

facts.fact: Nathan Ake could not continue after picking up an injury in Fenerbahçe's Champions League draw with Slavia Prague, reported a day before derby preparations began.
facts.meaning: Fenerbahçe may also be without a defensive regular at RAMS Park — his fitness is the biggest open question on their team sheet.

facts.fact: Fenerbahçe are averaging 2.57 expected goals across their last five matches, including an 8-0 win over Eyüpspor.
facts.meaning: They create more than the hosts have managed over the same span, which is why the market gives them a real share of this derby despite being away.

facts.fact: The market's fair goal line for this derby is 3.15 goals, with the main total set at 3.25.
facts.meaning: This is priced as an open, high-scoring derby — over 3.25 is close to a coin-flip rather than a long shot.

facts.fact: On the Asian handicap the market's fair line is Galatasaray -0.21, with the main line at -0.25.
facts.meaning: Despite home advantage and the table gap, the market rates Galatasaray barely a quarter of a goal the better side — this is priced as a near-even derby.

sources.fact: Galatasaray won 4-2 away at Lille in the Champions League, coming from behind twice to claim their first points of the campaign.
After the Lille win, Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk turned his focus to the Fenerbahce derby.
Victor Osimhen scored against his former club Lille, his first Champions League goal this season.
The match is the Intercontinental Derby, one of football's biggest rivalries, with Galatasaray based on the European side of the Bosphorus and Fenerbahce on the Asian side.
Fenerbahce were denied a much-needed Champions League win when Slavia Prague came from two goals down to equalise late for 2-2.
Nathan Ake could not continue after suffering an injury in Fenerbahce's Champions League match against Slavia Prague ahead of the derby.
Turkish media criticised Fenerbahce after the Slavia draw, drawing comparisons with Sabah, who beat the Czech side 2-0 a week earlier.
Marco Asensio will be out for three months after knee surgery, having played through injury to help Fenerbahce.
